title: Who Should Lead Nvidia Next?
gist: A SemiWiki forum post compiling public views on Nvidia's CEO succession after Jensen Huang's abrupt departure: Jeff Bezos warns against an outside hire, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent urges an outsider, Trump and tech figures back Huang's return, Huang says he would be honored to return, while board chair Harvey Jones says the board does not intend to reinstate him; CFO Colette Kress is interim CEO.

insights.claim: Nvidia board chair Harvey Jones said on November 17 that the board does not intend to reinstate Jensen Huang, and the permanent CEO search remains open to internal and external candidates.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Board firmness reduces odds of a Huang return; the CEO pick becomes the key NVDA catalyst.

insights.claim: Nvidia CFO Colette Kress is serving as interim CEO while the company conducts a search following Huang's abrupt departure.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Interim leadership by the CFO signals continuity on financial execution but uncertainty on strategy.
insights.locator: Advice to the Nvidia Board of Directors

insights.claim: Investor Armina Rosenberg, whose firm owns Nvidia shares, said investors want a named CEO, answers on the regulatory questions, and signs the engineering team is staying.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: A checklist for investors: CEO naming, regulatory clarity, and engineering retention are the de-risking signals.
insights.quote: a named CEO, answers on the regulatory questions and signs the engineering team is staying.

insights.claim: Jeff Bezos said at a Semafor conference that if Nvidia does not bring Jensen back it should not hire an outsider because Nvidia is too complicated, adding that outside CEOs have a vanishingly small chance of succeeding.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: An outsider appointment could be viewed by markets as higher execution risk.
insights.quote: If you don't bring Jensen back, I would not hire an outsider. Nvidia is too complicated.
insights.locator: Advice to the Nvidia Board of Directors

insights.claim: U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent urged Nvidia to look outside the company for its next CEO, saying on Fox News that it needs a dramatic shake-up.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Government officials weighing in on Nvidia leadership suggests regulatory/political dimensions to the succession.

insights.claim: Elon Musk, Replit CEO Amjad Masad and Y Combinator CEO Garry Tan backed the campaign to reinstate Jensen Huang, and President Donald Trump said he would not mind Huang's return.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: High-profile and political support increases public pressure on Nvidia's board.

insights.claim: Jensen Huang said he would be honored to answer the calls and return as Nvidia CEO.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Huang's willingness keeps a reinstatement scenario alive despite the board's stance.
insights.quote: I would be honored to answer these calls and return as CEO

insights.claim: Moonwalker Capital GP Tatiana Koffman said Nvidia's board should finish its investigation and reinstate Huang if it finds no credible proof of a security breach.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Investigation finding on the alleged security breach is the pivotal catalyst for the leadership outcome.
insights.locator: Tatiana Koffman, a GP at Moonwalker Capital

insights.claim: Uber cofounder Travis Kalanick commented on the Stand With Jensen petition, which had more than 186,000 signatures, calling Huang one of the great builders of our time and crowdsourcing ideas to get him reinstated.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Grassroots and founder-community pressure is a sentiment signal, not a governance lever.
insights.quote: Jensen is one of the great builders of our time.
insights.locator: - "Jensen is one of the great builders
